name: Dromoland Castle
positioning: 16th-century castle hotel on a five-hundred-acre estate of parkland and woodland in County Clare, on the west coast of Ireland
best_for: Travelers who want estate pursuits such as falconry, fishing, archery and clay pigeon shooting
History lovers who want to stay within the original castle walls
Families wanting Deluxe Family rooms or a two-bedroom suite

facts.text: The castle is surrounded by five hundred acres of parklands and woodlands.
The castle's lineage dates back to Brian Boru, one of Ireland's last High Kings.
Estate activities include rowing, fishing, clay pigeon shooting and archery.
Each suite is individually designed and set within the original castle walls.
The Viscount Staterooms sit within the castle's oldest wing.
Deluxe rooms have views over the gardens and Dromoland Lough.
Deluxe Family rooms have two Queen beds and sleep up to two adults and two children.
The two-bedroom suite is connected by a private corridor and looks over Lough Dromoland.
The resort offers golf and a spa.
Suites have Burren Perfumery bathroom amenities.
Dromoland Castle is a member of Preferred Hotels Worldwide and Ireland's Blue Book Hotels.

highlights.text: Guests can meet an owl and walk through the forest with a hawk on their wrist.
The Queen Anne Courtyard rooms overlook a courtyard built in 1736 by Sir Edward O'Brien.
The Brian Boru Suite has a freestanding slipper bath, a four-poster bed and tall arched windows looking over the lake and woodlands.
Guests can tour the castle halls with a storyteller who shares tales of Dromoland's history.
The Cocktail Bar was once the O'Brien family's library, an octagonal room overlooking the castle lawns.

considerations.text: WhataHotel notes the rural County Clare location requires advance planning.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the luxury castle experience.
